title: China: Ensure Sophia Huang Xueqin’s Release and Guarantee Her Freedom from Arbitrary Restrictions
content:
As journalist and prominent #MeToo activist Sophia Huang Xueqin approaches the end of her unjust five-year prison sentence, we, the undersigned civil society organizations, call on the Chinese authorities to ensure her immediate release and guarantee that, once released, she can carry out her journalism and human rights work without surveillance, harassment, retaliation or other restrictions.

Sophia Huang Xueqin is widely recognized for her work on human rights and commitment to press freedom. She is a journalist and one of the most prominent figures associated with China’s #MeToo movement. For years, she reported on and advocated for gender equality and supported survivors of sexual harassment and gender-based violence.

In September 2021, Sophia was preparing to start graduate studies in the UK. However, she and a friend, human and labour rights activist Wang Jianbing, were arrested in Guangzhou, China on 19 September, and detained incommunicado for more than five months. While in detention, both Sophia and Jianbing were reportedly subjected to ill-treatment, with negative impacts on their health.

title: Freedom House Launches Ambassadors for Freedom Program, Names Five Leading Human Rights Defenders as Inaugural Advocates
content:
WASHINGTON—Today Freedom House launched the Ambassadors for Freedom program, a new global initiative bringing together a group of the world’s foremost democracy advocates to champion solutions to the 20-year decline in global freedom. Carolina Barrero, Nazanin Boniadi, Anaïse Kanimba, Vladimir Kara-Murza, and Anna Kwok will serve as the inaugural ambassadors. Ambassadors will work in partnership with Freedom House to spotlight threats to freedom, engage policymakers and the public, and inspire a new generation to safeguard democracy.

“Freedom House has always believed that lasting change is driven by courageous individuals willing to stand up for freedom, often at great personal cost,” said Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly. “These ambassadors are some of the world’s great champions of the power of freedom and speak from personal experience as targets of repressive regimes themselves. Their courage is an example to us all and we are thrilled to welcome them as Freedom House Ambassadors.”

Freedom House Ambassadors

title: Freedom House Adopts Case of Imprisoned Belarusian Civil Society Expert Tatiana Kouzina
content:
Washington, DC—Freedom House announced today that the Fred Hiatt Program to Free Political Prisoners has adopted the case of imprisoned Belarusian civil society expert Tatiana Kouzina.

“Freedom House is proud to stand with Tatiana Kouzina and fight for her release. As we have documented, Belarus’s political regime is one of the most repressive in the world, featuring rigged elections, severe restrictions on journalists and civil society, and a judiciary subservient to the country’s authoritarian President Alyaksandr Lukashenka, who has been in power since 1994,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House “It is tragic but not surprising that the Lukashenka regime would imprison experts like Tatiana, who could otherwise serve as an independent source of information and a credible voice of dissent. We call for Tatiana to be immediately and unconditionally released.”

title: An Open Letter to Chinese Communist Party General Secretary Xi Jinping
content:
Re: Human rights improvements ahead of September 24, 2026 visit to Washington, DC

We, the undersigned organizations dedicated to protecting and promoting human rights, democracy, and religious freedom, write on the occasion of your forthcoming visit to Washington, DC.  We urge that ahead of your arrival you agree to release prisoners of conscience, pledge an end to transnational repression, and commit to critical legal reforms, among other actions. Such steps would diminish criticism around the visit of your government’s human rights violations.

title: Freedom House and the R.T. Weatherman Foundation Announce Partnership to Advocate for the Release of Hong Kong Political Prisoner Joshua Wong
content:
Washington, DC, and London, UK—Freedom House and the R.T. Weatherman Foundation are pleased to announce a partnership to advocate for the release of Hong Kong prodemocracy advocate and political prisoner Joshua Wong. As part of this work, Freedom House’s Fred Hiatt Program to Free Political Prisoners is formally adopting Wong’s case.

Joshua Wong is a prominent leader in Hong Kong’s prodemocracy movement whose activism has received international attention and acclaim. He co-founded the student group Scholarism, was a key leader in the 2014 Umbrella Movement protests in which Hong Kongers demanded free and fair elections, and co-founded the prodemocracy political party Demosistō. As a result of his activism, he has been imprisoned several times, including continuously since November 2020. On September 2, he is expected to plead guilty to charges under Hong Kong’s notorious National Security Law, which has contributed to the rapid deterioration of basic freedoms in the territory.
